evidence_levels.documented: stated in a cited source (Verne's reported words, firsthand observation, or reliable reference)
evidence_levels.inferred: reasoned from multiple sources; see reasoning
evidence_levels.speculative: plausible but weakly or not supported by collected sources

records.claim: Dearest and most intimate friend since childhood; co-explorer of the Loire; navy officer; companion on yacht cruises.

citations.quote: he is not only my brother but my most intimate friend

records.claim: Admired as cultured, literary and unambitious; provided Verne a small allowance in Paris.
records.caveats: Their extensive correspondence (letters from Paris 1848-1860s) is the key gap: not in corpus.

citations.quote: Our father, who was an admirable man
I was living then on a small pension allowed me by my father

records.person: Honorine Verne (née Morel, widow de Viane)
records.claim: Lively, proud of her husband, acted as hostess and gatekeeper (autograph requests); Verne credited her role in his success.
records.caveats: Modern biographers describe tensions in the marriage; not evidenced in corpus.

citations.quote: Mme. Jules Verne has played no small part in each and all of her husband's triumphs
If I were not there to save him from his friends

records.claim: Only child; lived in Paris, married with children by 1893; wrote on scientific subjects; later edited/revised posthumous novels.

citations.quote: He writes ably on scientific subjects

records.claim: Verne said he owed Dumas fils his 'deepest debt'; Dumas introduced him to Dumas père, co-wrote Pailles rompues, and proposed him for the Académie.

citations.quote: the friend to whom I owe the deepest debt of gratitude and affection is Alexandre Dumas the younger
Fifteen years ago Dumas proposed my name for the Academy

records.claim: Publisher of the Voyages extraordinaires; Verne called father and son 'my very good friends'. Hetzel was also editor/counsellor.
records.caveats: Hetzel's heavy editorial interventions (e.g. Paris au XXe siècle rejected; Nemo's backstory) are known from correspondence not collected.

citations.quote: this excellent man and his son became, and have remained, my very good friends
qui fut son conseiller en même temps que son éditeur

records.claim: Wrote operettas and songs with him (e.g. 'Les Gabiers').

citations.quote: Les Gabiers, par Jules Verne et Aristide Hignard

records.claim: Verne was intimate with Delibes ('we used to say thou') and friendly with Massé.

citations.quote: and so was Delibes, with whom I was very intimate

records.claim: Co-wrote the successful stage adaptations of Le Tour du monde and Michel Strogoff.

citations.quote: both dramas being written in conjunction with Adolphe d’Ennery

records.claim: Interviewed him (1893) and interpreted at Nellie Bly's 1889 visit.

citations.quote: Mr. Sherard in an attractive, lazy voice translated

records.claim: Received thousands of letters from Americans each year and professed great affection for America.

citations.quote: I do so love America and the Americans
There is one man in California who has been writing to me for years

records.claim: Malot called him 'the best of best fellows' (as quoted by Sherard).

citations.quote: He is the best of best fellows
